Implementation Plan

Scope-mode: Hold Scope  
Reuse-audit: extends `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` and `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh`  
Scope-mode justification: The complete fix includes both credential-free diagnosis and a separate issue-writing job; changing only the Codex sandbox flag would leave checkout credentials accessible. This follows `unattended_system_instructions.md` §6: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed. The extra job is necessary, not an optional expansion.

## Execution and automation

- **Change type:** Extend existing scripts and the reusable workflow; introduce no standalone script or supervisor.
- **Entry point:** Keep the existing `check_run: completed` caller in `.github/workflows/internal-check-failure-triage.yml` and the consumer wrapper’s existing trigger. Split the work inside `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml`; no operator invocation or removal-registry entry is needed.
- **Planning ref:** `main` at `9800a21ebff1f5fd5279ab423522879c5b5165f4`. No integration branch was specified, so no mismatch is established.

## Files likely to change

- `.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml` — separate diagnosis and publication jobs, restrict credentials, and transfer only the diagnosis.
- `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` — separate read/diagnose work from deduplication, lineage, and issue-writing work while retaining existing markers and limits.
- `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` — extend only where needed to support triage’s model invocation; reuse its snapshot, container, and broker rather than building a second isolation mechanism.
- `tests/test_check_failure_triage_workflow_security.py` — extend workflow and adversarial boundary checks.
- `prompts/mode-check-failure-triage.txt` and `agents.md` — correct the checkout-access description and document the resulting architecture.
- `changelog.d/6195-isolate-check-triage.md` — record the security change.

**Representative pattern:** `scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh` snapshots screened source without `.git`, then runs Codex in a read-only, network-isolated container through a host-side provider broker. Reuse its existing Dockerfile and `clarify_openrouter_broker.py`; do not mount the live checkout, runner home, or runtime directory into the model container.

## Functions or modules to implement

1. Give `check_failure_triage.sh` explicit diagnosis and publication paths. Diagnosis gathers the existing PR/check context and produces Markdown, but performs no label or issue writes. Publication reuses the existing lineage cap, open-issue deduplication, markers, issue composition, and notifications.
2. Run diagnosis with the existing isolated helper instead of host Codex’s `--sandbox danger-full-access`. Its failure must retain the current *inconclusive/raw-evidence* fallback, but must never fall back to unrestricted host Codex.
3. In the workflow, use a read-only token for diagnosis API calls and `persist-credentials: false` on checkouts. Give the model only a screened source snapshot and prompt; keep the OpenRouter key in the host broker. Checkout normally persists authentication unless that option is disabled. ([github.com](https://github.com/actions/checkout/blob/main/README.md?utm_source=openai))
4. Upload only the bounded diagnosis Markdown as a short-lived, run-specific artifact. Have a separate publication job download it, validate that it is a regular file within size limits, recheck the PR and deduplication state, and then perform writes. A missing or invalid artifact fails closed; artifact contents are never sourced or executed. GitHub documents same-run artifact transfer via upload/download actions. ([github.com](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/blob/main/README.md?utm_source=openai))
5. Keep `GH_PAT` out of the diagnosis job and scope it to the publication step. The publisher must use a clean trusted-support checkout, not execute the PR-head checkout. Retain PAT-backed issue creation because events produced using `GITHUB_TOKEN` ordinarily do not start the downstream clarification workflow. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow?trk=public_post_comment-text&utm_source=openai))

## Data structures affected

The diagnosis artifact contains Markdown only, not credentials, raw runtime files, or executable metadata. Preserve the existing issue-body fingerprint, generation, root, and PR markers and the existing lineage and duplicate semantics.

## API/interface changes

No new public endpoint or consumer input. Add an internal script mode and job handoff; preserve existing environment-variable names and provide defaults for any new helper option. The diagnosis job needs read access for the existing PR, issue, check-run, and job-log lookups; publication needs issue/label writes. Retain existing `gh_retry` calls, and document the publisher’s additional PR read: it cannot safely rely on metadata carried across the untrusted artifact boundary. Relevant contracts are `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}/check-runs`, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs`, `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels`, and `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs?source=post_page---------------------------&utm_source=openai))

## Decisions

### D1 — Isolate diagnosis and separate publication
- **Chosen:** Reuse the clarification container/broker for read-only diagnosis; publish from a separate trusted job.
- **Alternatives considered:** Unset token environment variables or change Codex’s sandbox flag in the current single job.
- **Why:** Neither alternative removes persisted checkout credentials or separates model-controlled work from privileged API writes.

### D2 — Transfer only diagnosis text
- **Chosen:** Pass one bounded Markdown artifact and rederive authoritative PR, lineage, and deduplication data in the publisher.
- **Alternatives considered:** Pass a complete PR/API-state bundle between jobs.
- **Why:** The artifact is untrusted output; it must not authorize a write or become executable input.

## Security considerations

Trust boundaries are PR-head files, PR descriptions and check logs → model snapshot/prompt → diagnosis artifact → privileged publisher. Restrict the container to screened regular files, read-only mounts, no network, no Docker socket, and the existing fixed-destination broker; never forward GitHub or provider credentials into it. Validate workflow inputs before checkout, artifact type/size before publication, and live PR origin/state before writes. Grant only read permissions to the diagnosis job and reserve issue-writing authority for publication. Abuse cases to test include prompt-injected exfiltration requests, tracked symlinks toward `.git` or runner files, a hostile artifact filename/content, stale PR metadata, and a broker or container failure. Job-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions support limiting the read job independently of the writer. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax?utm_source=openai))

## Risks and edge cases

- **Current-code conflict with the desired boundary:** `check_failure_triage.sh:322–331` invokes unrestricted host Codex, and `check_failure_triage.yml:219–259` checks out the PR and support with `GH_PAT` without disabling persisted credentials. Both must change together.
- Keep support execution trusted: a missing required isolation helper must fail closed, not select PR-authored executable code or unrestricted Codex.
- Preserve the existing empty-diagnosis fallback, self-loop exclusion, generation cap, deduplication, smoke-alert silencing, and automatic issue-triggered pipeline.
- Limit artifact retention and contents; do not upload raw check logs. Isolation does not itself prevent sensitive text already present in logs from being quoted in an issue, so apply the repository’s existing redaction conventions before publication.

## Testing considerations

Extend the existing security test module to assert job permissions and ordering, `persist-credentials: false`, no PAT/model invocation in the wrong job, required isolation arguments and mounts, and publisher rejection of missing, oversized, symlinked, or malformed artifacts. Exercise injected PR descriptions/logs with mock Docker and GitHub calls; verify no host-Codex fallback, no publication after failed transfer, and unchanged deduplication, lineage, and fallback behavior. Run the existing CI security-test step and workflow/shell validators on the repository’s pinned tooling; check workflow byte size after editing.

## Pre-execution self-check

The plan covers the reported credential path, preserves automated scheduling, identifies the privileged handoff, and requires no unavailable scalar input. No repository files were modified during planning.
